newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Hi-Bred sees '97 EPS around $2.90.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Hi-Bred sees '97 EPS around $2.90.

text.p: Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc said Wednesday it expects fiscal 1997 earnings to fall in the middle of the range of $2.70 to $3.10 a share.
"We feel comfortable that 1997 results will be toward the middle of that range," Chairman Charles Johnson said in a statement.
In mid-June Pioneer said it was comfortable with the same range of estimates .

The seed and agricultural genetics company today reported earnings for the third quarter ended May 31 of $4.04 a share, up from $3.64 a year ago. For the first nine months, it earned $3.46 a share, up from $3.10 a year ago.

In a statement, Johnson said fourth quarter results may not match the fourth quarters of the previous two years because late planting in 1995 and 1996 delayed some sales to the fourth quarter in those years. In the 1996 fourth quarter Pioneer lost $0.42 a share. In the 1995 fourth quarter it lost $0.59 a share.
It said this year's fourth quarter will be impacted by uncertainty in sales for operations in Latin America.
While long-term prospects are good for that region, 1997 results may be affected by the timing of the supply of new genetics, it said.
Pioneer said its leading North American share of the hybrid corn seed market appears to be 42-42.5 percent, down 1.5-2.0 percentage points from the previous year.
"Our 1997 market share was affected by several factors, including the transition to our new lineup of genetics," Johnson said.

"We will have large supplies of high-yielding new genetics in 1998. We are very encouraged by the potential of the new lineup, which includes several new hybrids with resistance to European corn borer, high oil hybrids and other specialty hybrids," he said.
Pioneer expects to build its North American corn market share in the coming years, he said.

Looking ahead to 1998, Johnson said there was a "high level of excitement" at Pioneer for new products released in limited volumes in 1997. He said about 40 percent of next year's corn hybrid sales in North America will be from products released in 1997. In a typical year, about 10 percent of Pioneer's hybrid seed corn lineup is in newly released products, he added.
